title: Topic 7.2: Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading

pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 7.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: INDEPENDENT READING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.2: Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why should we read different types of materials?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read a variety of materials (narratives, poems, graded readers) for lifelong learning
2. demonstrate independent reading of a variety of materials (narratives, poems, graded readers) for information

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. read a variety of materials (narratives, poems, graded readers) for lifelong learning
   In simple words: practise until you can read a variety of materials (narratives, poems, graded readers) for lifelong learning. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. demonstrate independent reading of a variety of materials (narratives, poems, graded readers) for information
   In simple words: practise until you can demonstrate independent reading of a variety of materials (narratives, poems, graded readers) for information. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
4. Show that you can: read a variety of materials (narratives, poems, graded readers) for lifelong learning

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading important for a Grade 4 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Set up an after school club where they meet on a regular basis to read extensively,
2. Retell the stories they have read in pairs or groups,
3. Communication and Collaboration: This is developed as the learner exchanges ideas during school reading clubs.
4. Learning to Learn: This is enhanced as the learner sources for information on their own. 52 Values:
5. Respect: It is developed as the learner appreciates opinions of others when sharing reflections on the text

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we read different types of materials?
2. What kind of materials do you enjoy reading?
3. What can you do to remember what you read?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. read a variety of materials (narratives, poems, graded readers) for lifelong learning
2. demonstrate independent reading of a variety of materials (narratives, poems, graded readers) for information

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
